newsitem.title: USA: U.S. soybean growers support China in WTO.
newsitem.headline: U.S. soybean growers support China in WTO.

text.p: U.S. soybean growers support China's accession to the World Trade Organization (WTO) but believe it must join on "commercially acceptable terms," the American Soybean Association (ASA) said Saturday.
The soybean grower group added a China resolution to their 1997 mission at a three-day convention here held jointly with the National Corn Growers Association.
ASA urged the Clinton administration to make expanded trade in oilseeds a "key priority" in China WTO negotiations.

"We feel its very important they become part of the WTO but not under just any circumstances," ASA chairman John Long told reporters. "They have to address their state trading regime and their import tariff regime and make it where soybeans have equal access to their markets with any other feed product."
China has been a huge buyer of soybeans and soybean meal recently.
Asked about spring acreage, Long predicted it would take a "pretty good swing in prices" to pull Midwest farmers out of a 50-50 rotation of corn and soybeans.
Last year's overhaul of U.S. farm policy removed most of the federal controls on what farmers could grow.
"What this flexibility is going to do, is it's going to allow people who maybe have not had the 50-50 rotation to get themselves more aligned to that," Long said.
Long said there could be an increase in soybean acreage in the South as farmers switched from cotton.
